thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: p99 latency breach detected for /v1/chat/stream (hosted-us-west) — auto-escalation to oncall

sara: I'm oncall. seeing alerts for p95 ~ 420ms -> 600ms and p99 trending to 2.3s. queuing up graphs now. any recent deploys?

lee: we just rolled a precision profile change for model 'redwood-open-7b' to enable int8 mixed-path on the serving fleet about 10m ago. change-id=rp-2026-03-15-74

marcos: confirming, network looks fine, resource saturation low. no infra CPU/GPU OOMs on the surfaced hosts.

ava: CS reported a customer timeout on streaming completions—quote: "responses intermittently stall and then catch up, UX awful". customer-id=acme-inc, started ~+8m ago.

priya: attaching quick p95/p99 from the last 30m: p95=620ms, p99=2.4s, stream-stalls spikes correlate with KV-cache-miss rate jump.

lee: past telemetry: after profile flip we saw an increase in dequant latency on some long-context workloads. suspect mixed-precision path for attention dequant step.

sara: can we confirm it's the precision change and not a model weight issue? any errors in serving logs?

lee: logs (snippet):
```
[2026-03-15T12:04:21Z] model=redwood-open-7b node=gs-12 path=int8 dequant_ms=18.2 kv_miss=true
[2026-03-15T12:04:21Z] model=redwood-open-7b node=gs-42 path=int8 dequant_ms=93.5 kv_miss=true
[2026-03-15T12:04:22Z] stream=abc123 stall=1250ms p99-path=slow
```
Not uniform across nodes — fallback appears required.

marcos: interesting that kv_miss is high on those nodes—could be cache eviction pattern for long contexts after the new op path changed buffer usage.

priya: impact assessment: ~4% of hosted production requests hit p99 > 2s in the last 15m. error-rate not increased but streaming stall durations have customer-visible delays. paging customers flagged: acme-inc, beta-hub, travelly.

sara: immediate mitigation: roll routing for redwood-open-7b in hosted-us-west to the f16-compat model variant (stable path) and throttle the int8 precision rollout. can ops flip routing?

lee: I can scale a canary rollback of the precision profile via infra API, command: 
```
redwood model-profile rollback --model redwood-open-7b --profile rp-2026-03-15-74 --to stable-fp16 --region us-west --force-canary 50
```
Executing now.

incident-bot: Action recorded: rollback started (canary 50% traffic) — change-id rp-2026-03-15-74-rollback. Notifying oncall and SRE.

marcos: routing change propagated to ~half of nodes in us-west. watching p99 now.

priya: metric snapshot 2m after rollback start: p95=380ms, p99=720ms, stream stall count down 60% from peak. good signal.

ava: pinging CS to notify affected customers: messaging drafted to ACME and co.

ava: "we observed transient delays tied to a precision optimization rollout, we've rolled back a portion of the change and are monitoring — apologized for the degradation." sending now.

sara: nice. can we do a full rollback or do a staged rollforward after root cause?

lee: recommend full rollback for hosted-us-west for safety, then re-run calibration offline with longer context replay tests. full rollback command: 
```
redwood model-profile rollback --model redwood-open-7b --profile rp-2026-03-15-74 --to stable-fp16 --region us-west --force 100
```
I'll queue it after confirming no other pending changes.

marcos: before full rollback, let's ensure dedicated customers on that profile aren't negatively impacted — checking dedicated pools.

priya: monitoring dedicated pools — no significant uptick in latency for dedicated tenants; issue concentrated on hosted routing where mixed packing interacts with KV cache.

sara: proceed with full rollback. lee execute when ready and call back once route convergence completes.

lee: executing full rollback now. ETA for routing propagation ~90s per zone.

incident-bot: Change completed: rollback to stable-fp16 for redwood-open-7b in us-west. change-id rp-2026-03-15-74-rollback (complete)

priya: post-rollback metrics (5m): p95=210ms, p99=310ms, stream-stalls returned to baseline. rolling close on paging.

ava: customers notified: ACME acknowledged and appreciated fast response. no immediate escalations.

marcos: root-cause hypothesis: the int8 mixed-path introduced a dequant code path that amplifies KV cache eviction penalties for long-context requests; certain nodes had a pathological buffer allocation leading to excessive miss amplification.

lee: follow-ups: run synthetic long-context replay against int8 path with KV stress, add a regression test to our profiling harness to catch >x% p99 delta for streaming stalls, and add a circuit-breaker to routing that auto-falls back when p99 delta > 50% in 5m windows.

sara: action items (assigned):
- lee: rerun calibration and synthetic replay, deliver test by EOD.
- priya: add auto-fallback rule to routing runbook and implement alert for KV-miss rate; PR by tomorrow.
- marcos: investigate node buffer allocation pattern and whether a kernel tweak can reduce dequant variance; start postmortem.
- ava: follow up with customers with summary and ETA for permanent fix.

priya: closing note: paging resolved, SLOs restored. will open incident ticket and schedule 1hr postmortem tomorrow 10:00.

sara: thanks team — nice quick coordination. :thumbsup:
